title: Fidan Sets Stage for Erdoğan's Landmark Syria Visit, Signaling $10B Trade Push and Deeper Strategic Ties
subhead: Turkey's foreign minister wrapped a two-day Damascus tour by announcing an Erdoğan visit is imminent, as Ankara and the new Syrian leadership finalize a strategic energy document, target $10 billion in annual trade, and activate a Joint Higher Committee. Domestically, a senior AKP lawmaker publicly floated the parliamentary mechanism seen as a path to a fourth Erdoğan term.

sections.heading: Erdoğan's Syria Visit Set as Ankara and Damascus Deepen Institutional Ties
sections.body:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan will visit Syria 'in the near future', Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said after a two-day trip to Damascus, according to The New Arab. Fidan met Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa, Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Interior Minister Anas Khattab, and said preparations for Erdoğan's visit were part of the talks. The visit is not yet formally confirmed.

Fidan said the two sides reaffirmed 'the common determination to preserve Syria's unity and territorial integrity' and discussed activating a Joint Higher Committee to oversee political, diplomatic, economic and security cooperation through specialized sectoral committees covering energy, refugee returns, education and culture. He also met a delegation of the Syrian Turkmen Council headed by Abdul Rahman Mustafa, per Anadolu Agency.
sections.whyItMatters: A confirmed Erdoğan trip to Damascus would be the most visible normalization milestone between Ankara and the post-Assad government, formalizing Turkey's role as the new Syrian administration's most consequential external patron.

sections.heading: Energy Strategy, $10B Trade Target Anchoring the Bilateral Agenda
sections.body:
Syrian Foreign Minister Shaibani said the two sides are working on a 'comprehensive strategic document' on energy and aim to raise bilateral trade to around $10 billion annually, The New Arab reports. He noted an energy agreement signed in May 2025 already facilitates electricity supplies across the border into northern Syria, and said broader talks cover gas, electricity and grid interconnection.

Fidan said Trade Minister Ömer Bolat recently visited Damascus and Aleppo with a business delegation focused on investment and trade, particularly in energy. He also framed Syria as a potential transit corridor connecting Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Gulf states and Iraq with Turkey and the Mediterranean — a role that could grow if regional shipping patterns shift amid pressure on Gulf routes.
sections.whyItMatters: The energy dossier moves from crisis-era electricity patches to a structural gas and grid strategy, positioning Turkey as the link connecting Gulf producers to European and Mediterranean markets.

sections.heading: AKP Lawmaker Floats Parliamentary Path to Another Erdoğan Term
sections.body:
A senior AKP lawmaker publicly detailed the constitutional route to a further Erdoğan candidacy. Abdulhamit Gül, AKP parliamentary group deputy chair, said at a news conference in Sakarya that a parliamentary decision — rather than a presidential decree — could let Erdoğan run again, Turkish Minute reported, citing state-run Anadolu Agency.

Under Article 116 of the constitution, if parliament calls early presidential and parliamentary elections during a president's second term, the incumbent may seek another term. The move needs 360 of 600 lawmakers. The ruling AKP and ally MHP lack that number, meaning support from other parties would be required. Gül also reiterated the push for a new, civilian constitution without explicitly saying it should lift the term limit. Erdoğan has governed since 2003.
sections.whyItMatters: This is the clearest official signal yet that Ankara is preparing the legal scaffolding for a 2028 Erdoğan bid, forcing the opposition to confront the constitutional mechanics now rather than after an election is called.

sections.heading: Economy: October Rate-Cut Calculus Complicated by Oil Volatility
sections.body:
Turkey's monetary path toward a possible October rate cut has become harder to read as oil prices stay volatile, Türkiye Today reported. With global crude under $90 after the US-Iran strike pause, per Reuters-linked headlines, the disinflation case has softened on the energy-import side, but the central bank must weigh the balance-of-payments and inflation effects of a still-uncertain regional market.

Separately, authorities seized 17.75 billion lira from illegal betting networks across eight provinces, per SCCG Management citing local reports, while NPR noted government concern that household gold hoarding ('under the pillow') is hampering financial intermediation — a recurring theme in Ankara's push to draw savings into the formal system.
sections.whyItMatters: The rate question is now hostage to energy prices: every sustained move in crude shifts the central bank's room to ease without reigniting inflation, keeping markets alert to the next oil headline.

sections.heading: LGBTQ Crackdown Draws Coordinated International Condemnation
sections.body: International rights bodies escalated pressure over the nationwide campaign against LGBTQ groups. Amnesty International called on Turkish authorities to end the 'escalating crackdown' on LGBTI rights organizations and release detained activists, and ILGA-Europe urged Ankara to stop the coordinated campaign against LGBTI+ civil society, European AIDS Treatment Group reported. The statements follow police tear-gassing of protesters in Izmir earlier this week.
sections.whyItMatters: The diplomatic push adds external cost to the domestic campaign, but with no sign of policy reversal, the pressure is unlikely to alter the government's approach in the short term.

sections.heading: Syria at Risk of Collateral Damage From US-Iran War — Think Tank Warning
sections.body: As Washington and Tehran pause strikes, Just Security warned that Syria's fragile recovery risks becoming 'collateral damage' in the US-Iran war. The analysis highlights how the regional conflict could disrupt reconstruction, sanctions relief and the very stability Ankara now seeks to lock in with Damascus — a reminder that Turkey's Syria project operates inside a wider, uncertain regional security picture.
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey's deepening investment in Syria is exposed to US-Iran escalation that Ankara does not control, complicating the 'safe, stable and prosperous' state Fidan described during his visit.

bottomLine: The dominant storyline is Turkey's accelerating embrace of post-Assad Syria: Fidan's Damascus tour and the imminent Erdoğan visit signal a transition from transactional support to institutional partnership, anchored by a strategic energy document and a $10 billion annual trade target. Domestically, the AKP has gone public with the constitutional mechanism that could extend Erdoğan's tenure past 2028, opening a new political front. The economy waits on oil prices before committing to October easing, and Ankara's LGBTQ campaign absorbs growing international criticism. Going forward, the Erdoğan-Syria visit — and the energy corridor it would formalize — is the development most likely to reshape Turkey's regional posture.
sources: The New Arab, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency, Turkish Minute, Türkiye Today, NPR, SCCG Management, Amnesty International, ILGA-Europe/European AIDS Treatment Group, Just Security
